LESSON: COMPOUND PROPORTIONS AND RATES OF WORK

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers 1.2 Cubes and Cube Roots (5 Lessons) • Cubes of numbers by multiplicatio
Topic 1.4: Compound Proportions and Rates of Work

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Compound Proportions and Rates of Work. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. divide quantities into proportional parts in real-life situations
2. calculate rates of work in real-life situations
3. appreciate the use of compound proportions and rates of work in real-life situations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: COMPOUND PROPORTIONS AND RATES OF WORK
Compound Proportions and Rates of Work is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Compound Proportions and Rates of Work problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Compound Proportions and Rates of Work question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Compound Proportions and Rates of Work question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Compound Proportions and Rates of Work set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Compound Proportions and Rates of Work.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Compound Proportions and Rates of Work in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. divide quantities into proportional parts in real-life situations
2. calculate rates of work in real-life situations
3. appreciate the use of compound proportions and rates of work in real-life situations

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
